program: Sound checkpoint, then electricity, magnetism and gravity-claim discrimination

provenance.independence: Separate model agents and independent calculations; correlated model-family authorship, not human peer review or historical-person participation.

reviews.title: A simultaneous reference can identify common gain drift
reviews.question: Under a shared scalar exponential acquisition gain, does a nondecaying simultaneous reference identify the target decay, and which physically different rival still survives?
reviews.scope: Known stable reference, ideal separated channels, shared scalar gain, physical-time premise. Generated PCM16, not physical recording.
withheld: Reference stability and shared gain are premises, not identified from corrected residuals.
Differential gain or unstable reference restores a nontrivial kernel; exact same-PCM examples with alpha 4 and 5 per second were executed.
The two channels already separate the signals; a one-microphone decomposition is not demonstrated.
Generated stereo PCM and digital full scale are not measured pressure, physical damping or energy.
No noise coverage or empirical calibration threshold was established.
reviews.finding: A stable shared-gain witness recovers the stipulated decay; differential gain and reference drift retain a one-per-second bias.
reviews.nextDecision: R1B: independent rank/kernel, quantized-file and different-alpha rival checks

reviews.title: A correction needs a full uncertainty budget
reviews.question: Can bounded positive envelope observations produce a rigorous slope interval, and how do stated reference/drift limits change the physical-alpha interval?
reviews.scope: Supplied positive envelope error boxes with declared reference/drift bounds. Not a statistical confidence interval.
withheld: This is deterministic interval arithmetic, not a confidence interval or an empirical coverage claim.
The supplied envelope-error guarantee does not follow from a recorded waveform, an AGC setting or a low residual.
A physical-alpha interpretation also assumes a single exponential, shared physical time and stated valid nuisance budgets.
The retained out-of-budget counterexample excludes true alpha; nominal width cannot compensate for a false bound.
The finite engineering ranges in these fixtures do not verify overflow behavior for arbitrary floating-point magnitudes.
reviews.incomingEvidence: R1B requires explicit reference and differential-gain uncertainty
reviews.finding: Precise envelopes give a narrow contrast box, but stated reference and gain uncertainty add 1.3 s⁻¹ to its width; missing bounds withhold a physical interval.
reviews.nextDecision: R2B: independent exhaustive interval endpoints, coverage and malformed-input checks

reviews.title: Electrical voltage gain is not net energy gain
reviews.question: Can an electrically resonant circuit show capacitor voltage amplification and source-off load work while its complete source/storage/loss budget remains passive?
reviews.scope: Ideal lumped RLC with series loop closed when source voltage is set to zero; signed electrical work and separately integrated losses.
withheld: A finite lumped linear simulation is not hardware calibration, empirical overunity testing or a proof about every electrical device.
Source off means ideal source voltage set to zero while the series loop remains closed; opening a physical switch would change this model.
Source waveform is sine starting at zero, stated explicitly in producer report.
Inductance/capacitance are constant here; moving geometry would add mechanical work and require a different boundary.
Numerical closure tolerance is not measurement uncertainty.
reviews.incomingEvidence: R2B required explicit complete nuisance budgets; subsequent user steering selected electricity/magnetism/antigravity and parked acoustic R3 before admission. Earlier atlas mechanical passivity was already known; new target is electrical readout and source-off boundary error.
reviews.finding: The capacitor approaches twice the source voltage while signed input work closes the energy budget; source-off load work is released storage, and reactive VA is not real power.
reviews.nextDecision: R3B: independent matrix solution and quadrature, phasor and omitted-storage controls

reviews.title: Magnetic support force needs source and mechanical work
reviews.question: Does a prescribed moving inductance yield an even-in-current upward force and smaller support reading while full electrical/field/mechanical energy still closes with unchanged g?
reviews.scope: Positive L(z), prescribed motion, maintained current and source-inclusive field/mechanical energy; static contact forces use unchanged g.
withheld: L(z) is a supplied finite-domain model, not a measured coil geometry.
The motion is prescribed; free dynamics, mechanical stage work and a moved load gravitational potential are not solved.
Static one-pan reduction assumes reaction support outside that pan. The independently derived complete static support sum cancels internal force only within the relative-coordinate model.
External fields, leads, heating, buoyancy and dynamic/field momentum remain possible measurement channels outside this model.
Current-even force is not a gravity identifier. No hardware, levitation or gravity change was measured.
reviews.incomingEvidence: R3B required motion-dependent source work and mechanical energy
reviews.finding: A 2 mN upward magnetic force reduces a 1 g pan indication with unchanged gravity; maintained-current source work supplies both field-energy increase and mechanical work.
reviews.nextDecision: R4B: independent coenergy/flux derivative, energy and stator reaction checks

reviews.title: Which observations could identify a gravity-like change?
reviews.question: Can paired-support and polarity-averaged observations across known masses recover a deliberately injected common acceleration change under a constant-bias model, and what exact rival still prevents an empirical gravity identification?
reviews.scope: Synthetic contemporaneous static support contrasts, paired polarity and known masses; injected common acceleration identified only under constant even-bias model.
withheld: Injected delta_g is a hypothetical shared model deformation, not an observed anomaly or proposed new force law.
Known calibration, simultaneous supports, common static g and mass/polarity-independent even bias are premises.
The expanded inverse has domain3, rank2, nullity1, kernel(1,0,-1); repeating the same readout cannot resolve it.
The2microN support bound is supplied, not measured detector sensitivity.
The1e-12 numerical guard is tested on these finite fixtures and is not a universal floating-point enclosure certificate.
External fields, thermal/mass-correlated drift, electrostatic forces, air motion, leads and real apparatus calibration remain unresolved empirical channels.
reviews.incomingEvidence: R4B independently verified stator reaction and selected paired supports, polarity, mass variation and a retained mass-proportional bias kernel.

repair.scope: Numerical outward padding only; frozen model/contract and theoretical bound unchanged.

reviews.finding: Paired supports and four masses recover a deliberately injected acceleration-like slope, but an exact mass-proportional ordinary bias reproduces every observation; unknown bias prevents a gravity conclusion.
reviews.nextDecision: R5B: independent error-box vertices, raw rival, rank/kernel and strict endpoint checks; preserve and repair the inward-rounding failure.

A mass-proportional ordinary bias exactly reproduces all raw observations, preventing empirical gravity identification without an independent bound.
reviews.nextDecision: STOP: no sixth research round. Future empirical work requires an independently characterized readout or bound distinguishing common acceleration from mass-proportional bias.
